title: Understanding Pause, Stop, Hide
takeaway: Moving or automatically updating content needs an effective pause mechanism.
decision: Provide an explicit film pause control, visibility suspension and reduced-motion support.

title: Intersection Observer API
takeaway: The browser can report visibility asynchronously without continuous scroll polling.
decision: Suspend the landing film outside the viewport and use lazy media loading.

title: Web Vitals
takeaway: Loading, responsiveness and visual stability jointly affect the experience.
decision: Bound parallel retrieval, reserve media dimensions and lazy-load card imagery; measure rather than claim a performance score.

title: Authorization Cheat Sheet
takeaway: Authorization belongs on each resource and action, with least privilege and explicit tests.
decision: Derive actors from verified JWTs for preferences, comments, bookmarks and notifications; test cross-account access.

title: Bringing Dark Patterns to Light
takeaway: Deceptive presentation can obstruct informed user choice.
decision: Keep preference controls, undo, reset and disclosure visible; do not fabricate urgency or social proof.

title: User Controls: Do YouTube’s Controls Work?
takeaway: The study found a gap between expected and actual effects of recommendation controls.
decision: Test that mute, hide and explicit feedback really change eligibility or order. ICO returned 403, so this readable original study replaces it.

title: DSA impact on platforms
takeaway: Transparent explanations and meaningful recommendation choices are emphasized.
decision: Explain actual ranking reasons and expose chronological and personalization-off modes. This is a design lesson, not a legal-compliance claim.

title: Evaluating recommender systems
takeaway: Recommendation outcomes require ongoing evaluation with different methods.
decision: Verify ranking properties and account isolation now; defer claims about retention or satisfaction until measured with users.

title: Privacy Without Monopoly
takeaway: Interoperability requires informed choice, data minimization and clear boundaries around shared information.
decision: Keep feed learning first-party and account-scoped; sharing starts from an explicit user action.

title: We should know all our data and profiles
takeaway: Inferred preferences can reveal information people did not knowingly provide.
decision: Show inferred interest provenance, support editing and history reset, and avoid outside tracking.

title: What Is News?
takeaway: Audiences bring different expectations about timeliness, relevance and what qualifies as news.
decision: Keep publisher, publication time and content format visible; do not label every video as verified reporting.

title: Constant Companion
takeaway: The youth-focused study describes notification overload and complicated benefits and costs of personalized media.
decision: Send only actual comment-interaction events, deduplicate notifications and keep read controls. Do not generalize the youth sample to every user.

title: Local audiences consuming news on social platforms are hungry for transparency
takeaway: Focus groups reported convenience alongside concern about opaque feed selection and data collection.
decision: Pair useful discovery with readable recommendation reasons and visible preference sources.

title: Digital News Report 2026: Overview and key findings
takeaway: Survey findings describe growing video-led news use alongside concerns about overload and trust.
decision: Offer relevant video alongside stories, preserve source links and keep viewing a deliberate action.

title: IFCN Code of Principles: The commitments
takeaway: Traceable evidence and transparent methodology let readers inspect conclusions.
decision: Retain original publisher links and distinguish ranking explanations from fact-checking or certification.

title: The 8 Trust Indicators
takeaway: Source identity, labels, methods, references, diverse voices and actionable feedback help readers evaluate news.
decision: Display publisher and format metadata and offer feedback without inventing a trust badge. Actual domain corrects the planned trustproject.org.

title: Website Rating Process and Criteria
takeaway: NewsGuard describes an editorial assessment with evidence-backed criteria, separate from user-platform content.
decision: Do not manufacture reliability scores from engagement; content reasons describe relevance only.

title: How we fact check
takeaway: Full Fact prioritizes public-interest claims, primary evidence and corrections.
decision: Keep original links accessible and preserve published metadata; no claim that this aggregator fact-checks every story. Search returned readable first-party article text although direct open returned 410.

title: Journalism Trust Initiative
takeaway: JTI evaluates journalism processes and transparency rather than determining the truth of each individual item.
decision: Keep relevance ranking separate from source certification; do not claim JTI participation.

title: The Trust Principles
takeaway: Reuters emphasizes independence, integrity and reliable information serving varied interests.
decision: Preserve publisher identity and source variety instead of optimizing only click counts. This readable official page replaces inaccessible reuters.com.

title: News values and principles
takeaway: AP describes standards for accuracy and avoidance of bias and conflicts of interest.
decision: Treat source attribution and original context as essential metadata; do not imply AP endorsement.

title: EXPIRE
takeaway: Expiration bounds how long cached data remains available, and update behavior must be understood.
decision: Use bounded cache and signal lifetimes with explicit invalidation. Redis is a research reference; this implementation uses bounded process caches and MongoDB TTL, not a Redis service.
